input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation for KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic remediates the KServe serving-stack images — the KServe components
and the serving data plane — so that they run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no
non-validated crypto in the request path. It delivers the remediated images,
the per-image crypto module inventory, and the FIPS test results that feed the
compliance evidence package.

## Scope

- Identify all non-validated cryptographic library usage linked into the
  KServe serving-stack images (KServe components and the serving data plane).
- Replace or rebuild against validated cryptographic modules so that no
  non-validated crypto remains in the request path.
- Verify that the serving stack functions correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  clusters in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- Record a per-image crypto module inventory and the FIPS test results for
  every remediated image, as the input to the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A binary/library scan of every remediated KServe serving-stack image shows
  no non-validated cryptographic libraries in the request path; all
  request-path cryptography comes from validated modules.
- The serving stack passes its functional test suite on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- Every remediated image builds green in its build pipeline.
- A per-image crypto module inventory and FIPS test results are documented for
  every image in scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules — this epic covers the KServe components and
  serving data plane images.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results for
every serving-stack image in scope (KServe components, serving data plane, and
Platform Operator) — and submits it through the security review board to the
external accredited certification lab.

## Scope

- Consolidate the per-image crypto module inventories, build attestations, and
  FIPS test results produced by the serving-stack image remediations into a
  single compliance evidence package.
- Drive the package through the required security review board milestone
  sign-offs.
- Submit the package to the external accredited certification lab and record
  the submission confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations, and
  test results covering every serving-stack image in scope, with no gaps.
- The package passes the required security review board milestone reviews.
- The complete package is submitted to the accredited certification lab with
  all required artifacts and milestone sign-offs, and the submission
  confirmation is recorded.

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited lab's historical turnaround is six to nine months, and the
  review board meets on a fixed cadence; both are externally controlled and
  cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They gate the certification
  outcome and the certification date, not this epic's deliverable (a complete,
  submitted package).
- Acceptance into the lab's review queue is granted by the external lab, not
  by this epic's work: it is the expected follow-on to a complete, compliant
  submission, and is tracked here as an acceptance expectation rather than an
  acceptance criterion.
- Re-split trigger: if module-inventory and test-result assembly outgrows
  roughly one sprint of effort, split the assembly work from the
  submission/review-board coordination work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds

## Description

This epic delivers a gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build whose
images reintroduce non-validated crypto usage, so that FIPS compliance cannot
regress once the serving-stack images have been remediated.

## Scope

- Implement a CI check that scans serving-stack build outputs for
  non-validated crypto usage, with the deny-list derived from the validated
  crypto module inventory established during the image remediations.
- Wire the check into the build pipeline for all serving-stack builds (KServe
  components, serving data plane, and Platform Operator) so that it gates
  merges/builds.
- Demonstrate the check's behavior against both a non-compliant build and the
  remediated images.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The check fails a deliberately non-compliant serving-stack build that links
  non-validated crypto in the request path (demonstrated on a known-bad
  sample).
- The check passes on the remediated serving-stack images.
- The check is gating for all serving-stack builds in the pipeline — a failure
  blocks the build rather than only reporting.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# FIPS support posture documentation

## Description

This epic documents the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and
the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters,
so that customers (notably public-sector) can configure and operate the stack
in a FIPS-compliant way.

## Scope

- Author new/rewritten documentation topics stating the FIPS support posture
  of the model serving stack.
- Document cluster prerequisites (FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters) and any
  configuration requirements for validated crypto module usage.
- Document the scope boundary: workbenches, pipelines, and training FIPS
  posture is covered by separate strategies, as is Common Criteria
  certification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving
  stack and the cluster prerequisites for enabling it.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  of the remediated serving stack (spot-checked on a FIPS-enabled cluster).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013

FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack.

## Triage Outcome

Not below-threshold: the strategy spans two components (KServe, Platform
Operator) and multiple distinct work streams (image crypto remediation in two
repos, compliance evidence assembly with external submission, CI enforcement,
substantive documentation). Not docs-only: code changes are required.

No Investigation epics: the strategy's Open Questions section states "None on
scope". The lab turnaround and review-board cadence are external schedule
constraints (recorded as risks on the evidence epic), not technical unknowns
that change which epics exist or what they do.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation for KServe serving-stack images | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation for Platform Operator images | Implementation | RHOAI Core Platform | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E005 | FIPS support posture documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P0 |

Note: the strategy omits an Impacted Teams table. Team assignments are
inferred: KServe from `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`
(owning team "RHOAI Serving"); Platform Operator and Documentation teams are
assumed from the component names (see Health Warnings).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 KServe image remediation] --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 Evidence package]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 Platform Operator image remediation] --> E003
    E001 --> E004[RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 CI FIPS regression gate]
    E002 --> E004
    E001 --> E005[RHAISTRAT-9013-E005 FIPS documentation]
    E002 --> E005
    E003 --> E005
    E004 --> E005
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | 13 (work-product dependency) | The evidence package's content (module inventory, build attestations, FIPS test results for the KServe images) is produced by the KServe remediation; the package cannot be assembled before the remediated images exist. |
| E002 → E003 | 13 (work-product dependency) | Same as above for the Platform Operator images in scope. |
| E001 → E004 | 13 (build-against artifact) | The CI gate's deny-list of non-validated crypto usage is derived from the module inventory established during KServe remediation. |
| E002 → E004 | 13 (build-against artifact) | Same as above for Platform Operator builds; the gate covers all serving-stack builds. |
| E001 → E005 | 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes what was built; blocked by every Implementation epic. |
| E002 → E005 | 11 (docs last) | Same. |
| E003 → E005 | 11 (docs last) | Same. |
| E004 → E005 | 11 (docs last) | Same. Edges into the docs-authoring epic do not trigger priority inheritance (docs-authoring priority exception). |
| No edge E001 ↔ E002 | 14 (different repos, parallel) | KServe and Platform Operator images live in different repos with no shared artifacts; the remediations run in parallel. |
| No onboarding chain | 20 (not applicable) | KServe is an in-platform component (architecture context exists, Konflux onboarded). Platform Operator is an existing canonical component in `.context/rhai-components.txt` whose images the strategy remediates — this is hardening of existing images, not provisioning of a new component (see Health Warnings). |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Priority-split analysis |
|-----|----------|---------|-------------------------|
| HLR-1 (serving-stack images run on FIPS-enabled clusters with validated crypto) | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E001, RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | Split by component/team boundary (Rule 1): KServe images and Platform Operator images live in different repos owned by different teams. |
| HLR-2 (compliance evidence package assembled and submitted) | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | Single cross-component work product; assigned to the serving-stack team with component KServe as the most-relevant canonical name (spans KServe and Platform Operator — see component mapping note below). |
| HLR-3 (CI enforces FIPS regressions) | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Split from HLR-1 as a distinct, deferrable feature: it edits CI pipeline configuration rather than image content, has independent user value (regression protection), and shares no data structure or build surface with the image remediation. |
| HLR-4 (documentation states FIPS posture and prerequisites) | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9013-E005 | Substantive new documentation topics (not incidental touch-ups) → separate docs-authoring epic (Rule on work-product type boundaries). Its P0 priority comes from the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter `priority: Critical` → P0), not from HLR-4's P2 label. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Component Mapping Notes

- `RHAISTRAT-9013-E003` (evidence package) spans the KServe and Platform
  Operator remediations; assigned canonical component `KServe` as the single
  most-relevant name for the serving stack.
- `RHAISTRAT-9013-E004` (CI gate) covers serving-stack builds across both
  components; assigned canonical component `KServe` as the most-relevant name.
- `RHAISTRAT-9013-E005` uses canonical component `Documentation`.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted
  Teams table, no Dependencies table, no per-component change/owner detail in
  Affected Components, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Decomposition proceeded with inferred team
  assignments and ACs derived from the HLRs.
- **Inferred team assignments**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table. The
  KServe assignment (RHOAI Serving) is corroborated by
  `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`, but the
  team assignments for the Platform Operator remediation epic (RHOAI Core
  Platform) and the documentation epic (RHOAI Documentation) are inferred from
  the component names — confirm with the component owners before scheduling.
- **External schedule gates**: the accredited-lab turnaround (historically six
  to nine months) and security review board cadence are externally controlled
  and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They are recorded as
  Risks/Notes on the evidence-package epic — not as acceptance criteria — and
  they gate the certification outcome, not any epic's start.
- **Platform Operator lacks an architecture-context file**: it is present in
  the canonical component list (`.context/rhai-components.txt`) and the
  strategy remediates its existing images, so it is treated as an existing
  in-platform component rather than triggering the new-component onboarding
  chain (Rule 20). Consequently `architecture_claims` is scored 0 for its epic.
- **Docs epic priority**: HLR-4 is P2, but the docs-authoring epic carries P0
  per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority Critical → P0).
  This is rule-mandated, not a priority inversion.
- **Re-split trigger (evidence epic)**: if module-inventory and test-result
  assembly for the evidence package outgrows roughly one sprint of effort
  (e.g. the image count grows substantially), split the assembly work from the
  submission/review-board coordination work.

## Tiered Delivery

The external certification process does not gate any engineering epic: every
HLR (FIPS-capable images, evidence package submitted, CI enforcement,
documentation) is deliverable without the lab's outcome, and the certification
result itself is outside the strategy's requirements. Engineering value
(remediated images, regression protection, documentation) therefore ships as
Tier 1 independent of the lab schedule; no Tier 2 dependency-gated epics are
needed and no DAG split is required. The only externally-gated item — the
certification decision — is a post-submission outcome tracked as a risk, not
an epic.
